import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set a style for better aesthetics
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    alpha=0.7,
    s=100, # Set a fixed size for markers for consistency
    palette='viridis' # Choose a color palette
)

# Apply log scale to the y-axis for price, as prices often have a wide, skewed distribution
plt.yscale('log')

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Camera Price (Log Scale) vs. Megapixels, Colored by Sensor Type', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD, Log Scale)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to avoid overlapping with data points
plt.legend(title='Sensor Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
